# @flatten-js/spatial-graph

> A 2D graph for line networks: nodes are points ([x, y] tuples), edges are straight segments. Built on graphology and @flatten-js/core. Use it to route along a network, snap points onto it, split and merge edges, and analyse its structure (junctions, dead ends, connected components).

Requires Node.js 22+. ESM and CommonJS, with types. `@flatten-js/core` is a peer dependency: install it next to this package.

```sh
npm install @flatten-js/spatial-graph @flatten-js/core
```

## Quick start

```ts
import { Point, Segment } from '@flatten-js/core';
import { SpatialGraph } from '@flatten-js/spatial-graph';

const graph = new SpatialGraph({
  segments: [
    new Segment(new Point(0, 0), new Point(10, 0)),
    new Segment(new Point(10, 0), new Point(10, 10)),
  ],
});

graph.getShortestPath([0, 0], [10, 10]); // Segment[] (2 segments); [] if unreachable
graph.findNearestEdge([4, 1]);           // Segment
graph.getJunctions();                    // NxPoint[] (degree > 2)
```

## Rules that prevent most mistakes

- Points are `NxPoint = readonly [x, y]`. Edges are `NxEdge = readonly [NxPoint, NxPoint]`. flatten-js `Point`/`Segment` are accepted where a method says so and returned by `getSegments`, `getVertices`, `getShortestPath`, `findNearestEdge`.
- Coordinates are rounded to `COORDINATE_PRECISION` decimals (default 0, whole numbers) to form node keys. Points that round to the same key are one node. If your data uses small units, scale it up before building the graph.
- The graph is undirected and simple. No parallel edges, no self-loops. Zero-length segments are skipped silently.
- Edge attribute `weight` is the segment length and is set automatically. Shortest paths use it.
- Queries on a point that is not a node return an empty value (`[]`, `null`, `{}`, `0`, `false`); they do not throw. These throw: `findNearestEdge`, `projectPointOnClosestEdge` (no edges), `getClosestNodeToPoint` (no nodes), `moveNode`/`moveNodes` (missing node).
- `SpatialGraph` extends graphology `Graph`. Prefer the point-based methods over raw graphology ones. For a raw node key use `getPointKey(point)` (e.g. `"10,0"`).
- Serialize with graphology: `new SpatialGraph().import(graph.export())`. `graph.copy()`, `graph.emptyCopy()` (nodes only) and `graph.nullCopy()` (graph attributes only) return a `SpatialGraph` with shallow-copied attributes. Copy options must keep the graph undirected and simple. Constructor option `allowSelfLoops` (default `true`) controls raw graphology calls; point-based segment methods always skip self-loops. `Graph.from()` returns a plain graphology `Graph`.

## API by task

- Build: `addSegment(segment, attrs?)`, `addSegments(segments, attrs?)`, `addVertex(point, attrs?)`, `union(other)`, `splitEdge(edge, point)`, `getSubgraph(attrName, value)`, `SpatialGraph.createCompleteGraph(nodes, isValid)`
- Read: `getNodes()`, `getEdges()`, `getSegments()`, `getVertices()`, `getJunctions()`, `getStubs()`, `getConnectedComponents()`, `getFilteredNodes(predicate)`, `hasPointNode`, `getPointDegree`, `getPointNeighbors`
- Nearest and routes: `findNearestEdge`, `getClosestNodeToPoint`, `projectPointOnClosestEdge`, `getShortestPath(start, end)`, `findPaths()`, `findIsolatedPaths(subset?)`, `getPathLength(nodes)`
- Edit: `moveNode`, `moveNodes`, `collapsePointInto`, `removeStubPoint`, `removeDegree2PointAndJoin`, `removeEdge(s)`, `removePoint(s)`, `removeSegment`
- Attributes: `getPointAttributes`, `mergePointAttributes`, `getEdgeAttributesFor`, `mergeEdgePointAttributes`, `getNodeLabel`/`setNodeLabel`, `getEdgeLabel`/`setEdgeLabel`
- Geometry helpers (package root): `findIntersection`, `findLineIntersection`, `isPointOnSegment`, `projectPointOnSegment`, `nearestPointOnSegment`, `pointsEqual`, `getPointDistance`, `simplifyPolylinePath`

## Recipes

Snap a point onto the network and connect it:

```ts
const [snapped, edge] = graph.projectPointOnClosestEdge([4, 3]);
graph.splitEdge(edge, snapped);
graph.addSegment(new Segment(new Point(4, 3), new Point(...snapped)));
```

Split two crossing edges at the crossing:

```ts
const crossing = findIntersection(edgeA, edgeB); // null if they do not cross
if (crossing) {
  graph.splitEdge(edgeA, crossing);
  graph.splitEdge(edgeB, crossing);
}
```

Remove dead ends, then join one chosen pass-through node (do not apply it to every degree-2 node: that collapses loops):

```ts
graph.getStubs().forEach((p) => graph.removeStubPoint(p));
graph.removeDegree2PointAndJoin([5, 0]); // merges the two edges meeting at [5, 0]
```
